title: Make Your Haircut Go Further: Practical Advice for Norwich Clients
description: Practical, easy tips from 3D Cutz to keep your haircut looking sharp for longer between visits to our Norwich barber.

content.heading: Wash and condition with purpose
paragraphs: Over-washing removes natural oils and makes hair limp, especially on shorter cuts. Aim to shampoo 2–3 times a week depending on how oily your scalp is, and use a light conditioner on the ends to keep hair manageable without weighing the cut down.
If you work out frequently or live in a hard-water area, use a gentle clarifying wash once a fortnight to remove build-up, then follow with a lightweight conditioner to retain shape and texture.

content.heading: Style smartly every day
paragraphs: Choose styling products that match your cut and hair type: matte paste or clay for textured looks, light pomade for slicker finishes. Start with a small amount and build up — too much product is the quickest way to make a cut look heavy and lose definition.
Use a comb or brush to rehearse the original lines of the cut each morning rather than restyling completely; that keeps edges looking crisp for longer between trims.

content.heading: Protect your hair while you sleep and live
paragraphs: Sleeping on a cotton pillowcase can create friction and frizz; try a smoother fabric or keep hair tidy with a loose silk scarf if you want to preserve shape overnight. Also avoid constant heat from hairdryers and straighteners — lower heat settings and a cooling blast finish help hold a cut's shape without damage.
Sun, chlorine and salt can change colour and texture. Rinse hair after swimming and apply a small amount of leave-in conditioner before long days outside to protect the cut and keep strands pliable.

content.heading: Do small home maintenance and know when to return
paragraphs: You can neaten sideburns and the neckline at home with a trimmer on a conservative setting but avoid major clipping unless you’re confident; small errors are harder to fix. Keep a fine-tooth comb and scissors for tiny snips of stray hairs rather than heavy cutting.

If you’re local to Norwich and prefer a professional tidy, pop into 3D Cutz at 19 Prince of Wales Road when the shape needs restoring — a quick tidy keeps the overall style looking intentional until your next full cut.
